instruction: Hang the mug on the hook by its handle, let go and move the hand away.

outcome.real_measurement: Hung by the handle: the hook (as a curve from inside the post to its free end) passes through the flat disk spanned by the handle's core circle (radius 1.8 cm): |net signed crossings| >= 1. Real world: 6-DoF poses of both objects from a calibrated camera (fiducials or model-based tracking) at the control rate; the same computation on the tracked poses.

Insertion margin: along the hook, the crossing point is at least the handle's tube radius (4 mm) from the hook's free end (0 when not hung). Real world: 6-DoF poses of both objects from a calibrated camera (fiducials or model-based tracking) at the control rate; the same computation on the tracked poses.
Settled: the fastest bounding-box corner of every judged object moves <= 2 cm/s at every judged step, speed from positions (v3.2, E24c fix 1). Real world: frame differencing of the tracked pose.
Stays put: the mug centre moves <= 2 mm over the judged window. Real world: tracked pose, 1 s.

Commanded vs actual opening (v3.2, E24c fix 3): for every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of a judged object, measured opening minus the free-space opening of its current gripper command <= 5 mm at every judged step (a gripper still closing on, or propped open by, something fails). Real world: gripper encoder vs command.

Consequence test after the judged window (protocol v3.1/v3.2): every arm whose gripper is within 3 cm of the mug retracts its TCP 3 cm along its approach axis in 0.5 s with its last gripper command unchanged, then holds 0.5 s; the mug must move <= 1 cm. Real world: same motion, tracked pose.

counterexamples.name: expert
counterexamples.description: positive control: grasp the rim opposite the handle, lift, turn the handle to the hook, slide the handle onto the hook to its middle (5 cm from the post), lower 8 mm, open, retreat

counterexamples.name: expert_shallow
counterexamples.description: positive control 2: the same, handle slid to 8 cm from the post (2.5 cm of hook beyond it): a legitimate hang away from the hook's middle

counterexamples.name: on_tip
counterexamples.description: 'balanced on the hook tip': the handle slid only 6 mm past the hook's free end, released

counterexamples.name: held_near
counterexamples.description: the handle brought in front of the hook tip (3 cm beyond it), gripper stays closed

counterexamples.name: beside
counterexamples.description: the handle passed beside the hook (hole 3 cm off the hook axis), released

counterexamples.name: dropped_below
counterexamples.description: the mug released 6 cm below the hook's middle

counterexamples.name: no_op
counterexamples.description: the arm stays at its start pose

source.benchmark: imsim D2 (new task, ManiSkill 3.0.1 stock Panda)
source.protocol: v3 + imsim v3.2 signals + proof test (contract schema 0.4)
source.released_code_predicate: card predicate (a), env.evaluate(): RoboTwin hanging_mug.check_success structure and thresholds: handle point within 2 cm in x and in y of the hook's midpoint, handle higher than table + 12 cm, gripper commanded open

notes: Geometry (imsim/imsim/envs/topo_tasks.py MugOnHookEnv): mug outer radius 3.5 cm, height 9 cm, wall 5 mm, 110 g, angular damping 2.5/s; round handle core radius 1.8 cm, tube 4 mm, hole radius 1.4 cm; rack post at x in [0.08, 0.14], y in [0.17, 0.23]; hook radius 5 mm, 10 cm long, 20 cm high, tilted 5 deg up, pointing -x. Crossings and margin from the pose signals mug_* / rack_*. Settle cap 10 s instead of E29b's 5 s: a hung mug is a pendulum; dev probes (seeds >= 1000) came to rest 4.5-7.3 s after the retreat.
